articles.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' sets new pre-sales record with USD 100 million in tickets sold worldwide; Robert Downey Jr, Chris Evans starrer eyes USD 1 billion opening
articles.summary: 'Avengers: Doomsday' is still two months away from its release, but the Marvel Studios superhero epic is already breaking records at the box office.
articles.body: 'Avengers: Doomsday' is still two months away from its release, but the Marvel Studios superhero epic is already breaking records at the box office.After becoming the first film to cross USD 50 million in advance ticket sales, three months before its release, the film has now reportedly hit the USD 100 million mark at the global box office, thus setting a new pre-sales milestone. The film, directed by Joe and Anthony Russo, has generated significant demand since advance bookings opened in July.'Avengers: Doomsday' advance booingsAs per reports, the film saw a boost in advance ticket sales, following the trailer releases and the re-release of 'Avengers Endgame: Encore' which featured new post-credit scenes that set the stage for 'Doomsday'. The return of the OG ensemble cast led by Robert Downey Jr, Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, has also reportedly been one of the deciding factors for the strong ticket sales in international markets.In Brazil and the UK, 'Avengers: Doomsday' has reportedly become the fastest film to cross USD 1 million in pre-release ticket sales. The advance booking momentum has been building steadily over the past month, with the film crossing USD 40 million in domestic pre-sales, achieving the feat 100 days before its release.'Avengers: Doomsday' eyes USD 1 billion opening weekendWith anticipation building up by the day, early box office projections have placed 'Avengers: Doomsday' on course for a massive opening weekend. According to early estimates, the film could potentially gross more than USD 1 billion worldwide on its box office debut, thus joining 'Avengers: Endgame' which also hit the milestone. The recent success of 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' has also set the stage for the film to cross the billion-dollar mark when it hits theatres this December.Beyond its opening weekend, the film has already sparked speculation that it could just become the first film to hit the USD 3 billion milestone. Some early predictions have suggested that 'Doomsday' could potentially reach the USD 3 billion mark worldwide if its theatrical run matches the unprecedented levels of audience demand currently being seen in advance sales.This could also set the film up to become the highest-grossing MCU film of all time and beating the 'Endgame' record to become the highest-grossing film of all time.'Avengers: Endgame' remains the benchmarkFor now, however, 'Avengers: Endgame' continues to hold the box office crown after surpassing 'Avatar' over the past weekend and set a new record by totalling an estimated USD 2.925 billion.'Avengers: Doomsday' release date and cast'Avengers: Doomsday' is scheduled to hit theatres worldwide on December 18, 2026. The film will face some competition at the ticket windows as it will clash with 'Dune: Part Three' that is also slated to release on the same day and will have an exclusive IMAX release.The star-studded cast of 'Doomsday' includes Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, Florence Pugh, Vanessa Kirby, David Harbour, James Marsden, Ian McKellen, Patrick Stewart, Tom Holland among others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: When Catherine Zeta-Jones Told Michael Douglas She Wanted to Be Monogamous, He Had to Break It Off with 5 Other Women
articles.summary: The actor recalls the moment his future wife gave him an ultimatum early in their relationship
articles.body:
Michael Douglas says Catherine Zeta-Jones gave him an ultimatum early in their relationship

He was newly separated from Diandra Douglas and dating five women in different cities

Douglas and Zeta-Jones married in 1999 and share two children together

Michael Douglas had a few calls to make when Catherine Zeta-Jones made it clear she wasn't interested in sharing him.

In his new memoir, One Helluva Ride , Douglas, 82, looks back on the early days of his relationship with Zeta-Jones, 57, and reveals that the actress wasn't interested in becoming another relationship in his rotation. If he wanted to be with her, she made it clear, he had to be with her exclusively.

"She told me she understood that I was a single guy who'd come out of a long marriage, but she would only be monogamous," Douglas writes. "'I'm not interested in dating you if you're dating other people. You can either continue with them or end it and be with me.'"

Douglas had a pretty simple response, though he needed a minute — or, more specifically, five phone calls.

"I told her wait here I have to make five quick calls. 'Five? You have to make five calls?'" he recalls.

At the time, Douglas was still newly separated from his first wife, Diandra Douglas , whom he split from in 1995. He had been seeing five other women, though he says he viewed the arrangement as relatively straightforward.

"Just after my marriage, I had been seeing five other women. They knew I was recently separated and in the process of getting a divorce," he writes. "I made sure they all lived in different cities, which felt like a respectful way to be non-monogamous."

According to Douglas, none of the women had asked him for something more serious or even questioned whether he was seeing anyone else.

"None of them asked for a commitment or even asked what else I was up to. I am sure they were seeing other people, too," he writes.

But once Zeta-Jones made her position clear, Douglas knew what he wanted to do.

"That day, I called each one to say I met somebody and would no longer be able to continue seeing them. They all took it well," he writes.

And just like that, five relationships were over and Douglas was all in on Zeta-Jones.

One Helluva Ride doesn't shy away from the romantic chapters that came before Douglas' life with Zeta-Jones. He writes candidly about his past affairs, including romantic entanglements with his Romancing the Stone costar Kathleen Turner and Basic Instinct costar Jeanne Tripplehorn .

By the time he met Zeta-Jones, however, Douglas was already completely smitten. He first saw her in an early screening of her 1998 film The Mask of Zorro , then happened to cross paths with her a few weeks later at the Deauville American Film Festival in France while he was promoting A Perfect Murder .

He asked his publicist to arrange a meeting over drinks, and he quickly found himself impressed by more than her beauty.

"She was smart, funny, unpretentious, and, yes, breathtakingly beautiful. She just seemed so confident and self-assured, too," Douglas recalls in the book.

Later, after a dinner with Zeta-Jones and her Zorro costar Antonio Banderas and his then-wife Melanie Griffith , Douglas was even more taken with her. There was just one problem: He admits he was "smashed" by the end of the night.

As he walked Zeta-Jones to the hotel elevator to say good night, Douglas blurted out what would become one of his most memorable lines: "I'm going to be the father of your children."

"It wasn't a cheap pickup line. It was the truth," he writes.

The pair went on to marry in 1999 and have two children, Dylan, 26, and Carys, 23 . Douglas also shares son Cameron , 47, with Diandra, 70.

Nearly 26 years later, Douglas' relationship with Zeta-Jones has only grown deeper.

"There's just an unknown at a certain point over time," he tells PEOPLE. "It goes beyond being attracted to somebody in this matter. It's just an unknown bond of being close and… a mutual respect."

articles.title: Shia LaBeouf’s wife Mia Goth files for divorce amid his legal turmoil
articles.summary: The two actors were married in 2016
articles.body:
Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf after 10 years of marriage, citing irreconcilable differences, and is seeking primary custody of their daughter Isabel.

The divorce filing comes after LaBeouf's ex-girlfriend, FKA twigs, settled a lawsuit against him, allowing her to speak freely about her alleged experiences of sexual abuse during their relationship.

LaBeouf is currently on probation after pleading guilty to misdemeanor battery charges following a drunken brawl in New Orleans, and has expressed regret for his past mistakes in his relationship with Goth.

Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf after 10 years of marriage.

The Pearl star, 32, filed the papers Tuesday night and cited "irreconcilable differences" as the reason, according to TMZ .

Although they have been legally married since October 2016, the former couple had a turbulent on-and-off relationship in the public eye for over a decade. After Goth and LaBeouf met on the set of Nymphomaniac: Vol. II in 2012, they tied the knot in Las Vegas in 2016 and broke up two years later. They then reconciled around 2020 and welcomed their daughter, Isabel, in 2022. Their date of separation is listed on the documents as July 28, 2025.

Goth is asking for primary legal and physical custody of Isabel, and is requesting to terminate the court's ability to award spousal support to either of the actors.

The Independent has reached out to representatives for Goth and LaBeouf for comment.

News of the filing comes just one day after LaBeouf's ex-girlfriend, singer FKA twigs, settled a lawsuit against the 40-year-old Megalopolis actor , meaning she is now free to speak about her alleged experiences of sexual abuse with him.

The lawsuit was settled after LaBeouf agreed to end the nondisclosure provisions from the former couple's settlement in December 2025.

Their long legal fight started in 2020, when Twigs accused LaBeouf of being sexually, mentally and physically abusive throughout their relationship, which lasted for about nine months in 2018. LaBeouf denied the allegations at the time.

The singer's attorney, Mathew Rosengart, said Wednesday in a statement shared with The Independent : "On the heels of Mr. LaBeouf's now dismissed, failed December 2025 arbitration against Twigs in which he sought money from her, this important victory completely frees her to discuss her experience, advocate for other women who might be less privileged, and freely support the charitable causes of her choice, which she was previously blocked from doing. To her great credit, Twigs stood up for something larger than herself, all female survivors of sexual abuse."

LaBeouf's attorney, Shawn Holley, said that the former Disney Channel star "wishes Twigs nothing but the best in her life and career and, to that end, has agreed to end their long-standing dispute."

"Twigs has spoken about this matter for years and there is now nothing to prevent her from continuing to do so," Holley told The Independent . She refused to comment on Goth's filing.

LaBeouf is currently on probation after he was arrested after getting into a drunken brawl in New Orleans in February. He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery charges in June and was sentenced to two years' probation, rehabilitation for alcohol abuse, sensitivity training and anger management classes.

The actor had moved to the Louisiana city after his separation from Goth, Page Six reported at the time.

In March, he spoke about his breakup with Goth in an interview on Channel 5 With Andrew Callaghan.

"We were deeply unhappy," LaBeouf said. "I made a lot of mistakes early on before we tried to have a baby. I had violated trust in a big, big way."

He said that their problems were "impossible" to fix, but that he still had love and respect for Goth. "We're in a good spot. I mean, this isn't new," he said. "We've been there for a while, we're trying to figure out co-parenting, and we're good. Even through all this, she gives me grace."

articles.title: Before Hollywood and global fame, Jennifer Lopez once slept at dance studio while pursuing her career: ‘I was homeless before I got famous'
articles.summary: Discover Jennifer Lopez's inspiring story of overcoming homelessness at 18 while pursuing her dreams in dance and acting, ultimately leading her to become a global superstar with a net worth of $400 million. Learn about her early struggles, family dynamics, and breakthrough roles in her rise to fame.
articles.body: Jennifer Lopez’s early career transition from the Bronx to Hollywood involved a period of sacrifice that she later described as being technically homeless. The singer and actress came from a middle-class background and worked her way up in the industry step by step; however, there was a brief time period when she had to stay in a dance studio to make ends meet.Jennifer Lopez once stayed in a dance studioDuring one of her old interviews with W Magazine, the singer opened up about how she faced homelessness at one point in her life when she was 18 years old. She shared, "I was homeless before I got famous. I was homeless.” She added that she and her mother fought about her future a lot and that her mother did not really support her decision to pursue the entertainment industry. While Lopez wanted to dance, her mother wanted her to go to college and get an education. The two fought too much to the point where Lopez revealed during the interview that she had to move out of her home. "My mom and I butted heads. I didn't want to go to college—I wanted to try dance full-time. So she and I had a break," she shared. Lopez added, “I told her, ‘This is what I have to do.'"Unable to stay at her parents' house and lacking the funds to rent a place in New York City, Lopez often slept on the sofa in her Manhattan dance studio. During the day, she would take intensive dance classes and go to auditions and later would return to sleep on the studio couch after hours.Jennifer Lopez’s big breakHer IG break came within the same year and helped her rise to the top. She first landed a job dancing in Europe in a production of Golden Musicals of Broadway and later toured Japan too. When she returned home, she booked ‘In Living Color’ and became one of the Fly Girls. However, this resulted in her leaving NYC for Los Angeles.Jennifer Lopez credits her parents for her successDespite the differences between her and her mother, Lopez still credited her parents as the reason why she worked so hard and actually made it in the industry. During the interview she opened up about how hard her parents used to work to make ends meet and to make sure that she had a good life growing up, which is what she applied to her work.Jennifer Lopez’s net worthAccording to Celebrity Net Worth, the singer and actress has an overall net worth of USD 400 million. From the Bronx to becoming one of the top stars in the Hollywood industry, Lopez has surely come a long way. After ‘In Living Color,' the star rose to fame after starring as Tejano singer Selena Quintanilla in 'Selena,' which earned her widespread acclaim and established her as a leading actress. She also appeared in ‘Out of Sight,' ‘The Wedding Planner,' and ‘Maid in Manhattan,' to name a few.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Zendaya’s rise to fame: How ‘Euphoria’ and ‘Spider-Man’ cemented the star as a rising force in the Hollywood industry
articles.summary: Explore Zendaya's incredible journey from her early beginnings in theater to her rise as a Hollywood A-lister, marked by iconic roles in 'Euphoria' and 'Spider-Man', and her relationship with Tom Holland.
articles.body: Zendaya, born Zendaya Maree Stoermer Coleman on September 1, 1996, has become one of the most successful stars in the Hollywood industry presently. From child star to Hollywood A-lister, she turned her life around and has now worked with the likes of Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Hugh Jackman, Javier Bardem, Rebecca Ferguson, Josh Brolin, and many others. Here is a look at her start in the industry along with her rise to one of the biggest stars in the Hollywood industry.Zendaya’s early lifeZendaya’s upbringing was heavily rooted in theater and acting, all thanks to her mother. While growing up in Oakland, California, her mother used to work as the house manager at the California Shakespeare Theater in Orinda. This is where the actress spent most of her childhood helping out, studying acting, and training in hip-hop dance groups and local theater productions, which all helped hone her skills in the arts.As for her education, she attended the Oakland School for the Arts and spent her time performing in Shakespearean plays like ‘Twelfth Night’ and ‘Richard III.' She also started working as a child model and commercial actor at the time, before she and her family moved to Los Angeles to give her career in showbiz a better chance.Zendaya’s breakthrough as child actressShe scored her breakthrough roles around 2013, landing her role as Rocky Blue alongside Bella Thorne on the teen show ‘Shake It Up.' This helped her solidify her footing in the industry and helped her also explore music as a profession. She also released her self-titled debut pop album in 2013, featuring the hit single ‘Replay.’Her next big project came with ‘Dancing with the Stars,’ where she finished as the runner-up at age 16. She was the youngest contestant at the time. She later returned to acting to star in and produce ‘K.C. Undercover,' one of her first roles as a producer.Zendaya’s film debut with ‘Spider-Man’In 2018, she finally scored her leading role in the film ‘Spider-Man: Homecoming’ opposite Tom Holland. The film was a massive success and launched the star right into global stardom. Around the same time, she also starred with Zac Efron in the hit musical ‘The Greatest Showman’ and went viral after it was reported that she did many of her own trapeze stunts in the film.Her role as Rue Bennett in ‘Euphoria’ made history in 2020 as she became the youngest recipient to win the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series. She won the award yet again in 2022. Following this, she starred in a lot of blockbuster hits, including the ‘Dune’ franchise, 'Challengers,' ‘Malcolm & Marie,' the ‘Spider-Man’ franchise, and ‘The Drama.'Zendaya and Tom Holland’s relationship timelineHolland and Zendaya met for the first time during the filming of the first ‘Spider-Man’ film, and right from the beginning they became close friends. Right from the start, rumors of the two being in a relationship started circulating; however, for the next couple of years, the two maintained that they were nothing more than good friends. In 2021, however, paparazzi photographed the co-stars sharing a kiss in a car in Los Angeles. Later that year, Holland publicly acknowledged their relationship in a GQ interview, sharing that they felt "robbed of their privacy." Since then, the two have maintained that their relationship is their private business and that they do not wish to share any aspect of it with the public.Around 2024, after attending events together on multiple occasions, Holland proposed to the ‘Shake It Up’ singer in an intimate, low-key setting over the 2024 holiday season. Zendaya made the engagement public when she debuted her diamond ring at the 2025 Golden Globes, sending fans of the couple into a frenzy. Since earlier this year, there have been rumors of the two getting married in a private ceremony, which were started by Law Roach, Zendaya’s designer, who had earlier shared that the two had already gotten married.Since then, Zendaya has not shared any statements about the topic. articles.title: David Bustamante vende un perfume cada 15 segundos: "No son mi mayor fuente de ingresos, pero podría vivir de ellos sin problema"
articles.summary: El cantante David Bustamante ha visitado este miércoles 'El Hormiguero' para presentar 'El Zorro', el musical que va a protagonizar en el madrileño teatro La Latina a partir del 25 de noviembre.
articles.body: El cantante David Bustamante ha visitado este miércoles 'El Hormiguero' para presentar 'El Zorro', el musical que va a protagonizar en el madrileño teatro La Latina a partir del 25 de noviembre. PABLO MOTOS. Estrenas 'El Zorro', ¿qué es lo que más miedo te da que falle en la primera función? DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Que no me acuerde del texto. Tengo pesadillas con eso. El resto ya es jugar, y encima me dan espadas, ¿qué más puedo pedir? Es durísimo el teatro musical, me parecen unos artistas compuestísimos los actores de teatro musical. PABLO MOTOS. Dices que tienes muchos dolores. DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Sí, me duele todo. Hoy he estado ensayando caídas y cuando te caes cincuenta veces, acabas bastante dolorido. Yo, además, tengo vértigo y hay una escena en la que El Zorro vuela, con un arnés, por encima del público, pero tengo tantas cosas en las que pensar, que no creo que me acuerde del vértigo. Ya me pasaba cuando era albañil y hacía tejados, que tenía que traer el jornal a casa y no podía pensar en el vértigo. PABLO MOTOS. Habrá niños y niñas, chicos y chicas, que vayan a verte al teatro y no sepan quién es Bustamante y vean solo a 'El Zorro'. DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Ya me empieza a pasar, como llevo tantos años, llegan nuevas generaciones que no tienen ni idea de quién soy. Luego hay chicos de otras generaciones que veo en los conciertos y que se saben todos los temas, no sé si me conocen por la velada o por qué, pero me escuchan y se quedan. PABLO MOTOS. Tienes catorce perfumes en el mercado, ¿si voy a tu casa me los encontraría todos? DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Sí claro, están en el baño. Me estoy haciendo una casa y he hecho una hornacina con luz led para poner mis perfumes. Hay quien pone los Grammy y yo, como no los tengo, pongo mis perfumes. Se vende uno cada quince segundos, eso es porque la gente sabe que hago buenas fragancias. Mis favoritos son el primero, 'Muy mío', y este último. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Podrías vivir solo de la venta de los perfumes? DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Sí, perfectamente. No es que sean mi mayor fuente de ingresos, pero podría vivir de ellos sin problema. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Qué tal el entrenamiento con la espada? DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Estoy todavía en ello, aprendiendo. Yo me he cortado a mí mismo en las rodillas, porque todavía no controlo y me creo que sí. PABLO MOTOS. Estás también de gira. ¿Qué te pasó en un concierto de la gira con una mantis? DAVID BUSTAMANTE. Sí, me quedan cuatro conciertos. En un concierto estaba cantando una canción de amor y una mantis religiosa que pasaba por allí se lo tomó muy en serio y se me quedó enganchada en la cremallera del pantalón.

articles.body:
Festival de Cinema Italiano no Brasil — Foto: Reprodução

Quem gosta de cinema italiano já pode colocar a data na agenda: a 21ª edição do Festival de Cinema Italiano no Brasil começa em 5 de novembro e reúne 24 filmes, entre produções inéditas e clássicos. A programação ocupa mais de 120 salas em 90 cidades brasileiras e segue até 1º de dezembro, com entrada gratuita.

Entre os destaques está Scherzetto (Travessura), novo filme do diretor Mario Martone, com Toni Servillo e o jovem Lorenzo Perrotta. Baseado na obra de Domenico Starnone, o longa acompanha o encontro entre um avô acostumado à solidão e seu neto pequeno, em uma convivência que coloca duas gerações em confronto.

Ao todo, são 14 filmes inéditos — alguns recém-exibidos no Festival de Veneza — e dez clássicos. A retrospectiva desta edição, batizada de "Itália em Cena", reúne obras em que cidades, ilhas e paisagens costeiras italianas têm papel importante nas histórias. E quem preferir o sofá também poderá assistir a parte da seleção por streaming, gratuitamente, de qualquer lugar do Brasil.

articles.title: Juliana Linhares faz em janeiro, no Rio, a gravação audiovisual do show 'Até cansar o cansaço', destaque de 2026  | G1
articles.body:
Juliana Linhares na estreia do show 'Até cansar o cansaço', em julho, no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

♬ Um dos melhores shows de 2026 – e dos últimos anos – vai ser eternizado em 2027. Juliana Linhares fará a gravação audiovisual do show “Até cansar o cansaço” em 19 de janeiro, no Circo Voador (RJ), na volta da turnê ao Rio de Janeiro (RJ), cidade onde o espetáculo estreou em 16 de julho, entronizando a cantora potiguar como uma das maiores artistas do Brasil na atualidade pela força do canto teatral da intérprete e pela alta qualidade do repertório autoral da ascendente compositora.

O registro audiovisual do show “Até cansar o cansaço” será feito pela artista com convidados ainda não revelados, todos sob a direção musical do multi-instrumentista Elísio Freitas, arranjador do show e guitarrista da banda formada por Julia Rodrigues (bateria), Lucas Videla (percussão), Paloma Ronai (sanfona) e Nathanne Rodrigues (baixo).

Derivado do segundo álbum solo da cantora e compositora, também intitulado “Até cansar o cansaço” (2026) e lançado em 8 de maio, o show abarca no roteiro músicas como “Tesoura do desejo” (Alceu Valença, 1991) e “Chama da criança” (Juliana Linhares e Demarca, 2024), música do último álbum da banda Pietá, na qual a cantora foi revelada.

No show “Até cansar o cansaço” , assim como no álbum homônimo, Juliana Linhares dá voz a repertório que capta o estado de ansiedade e exaustão da humanidade no suor da lira incessante da era digital.

Michael Douglas claims Kobe Bryant would "stop by" wife Catherine Zeta-Jones' house 'a lot' before marrying Vanessa.

The L.A. Lakers superstar and Mark of Zorro actress were neighbors in the late 1990s when she was dating Douglas.

The couple got engaged in December 1999, five months before Bryant proposed to Vanessa.

Back when Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones were newly dating, and trying to make their long-distance relationship work, the actor had competition closer to home: her neighbor, Kobe Bryant .

After meeting in France in 1998, the couple struggled to spend time together as Douglas was based in New York and the 29-year-old Mask of Zorro actress lived in Los Angeles. "She had a house in the Palisades, right below Kobe Bryant's," the Fatal Attraction star writes in his new memoir, One Helluva Ride .

At the time, the L.A. Lakers superstar hadn't yet met Vanessa Laine, who would become his wife two years later in 2001.

"Apparently Kobe kept finding excuses to stop by Catherine's house," recalls Douglas, who is 25 years older than the Chicago actress. "I'm not sure how many times he 'lost his dog,' but it was a lot!"

Zeta-Jones' film career was on the rise, and productions like Sean Connery's Entrapment and High Fidelity with John Cusack kept her away from L.A. (and Bryant). "But we started talking on the phone pretty regularly," says Douglas, "until we could finally see each other again."

The couple got engaged on New Year's Eve 1999, five months before Bryant proposed to Laine in May 2000.

Zeta-Jones reflected on her time as Bryant's neighbor when the five-time NBA champion and his 13-year-old daughter Gianna were tragically killed in a helicopter crash on Jan. 26, 2020, along with seven others all on their way to a basketball game.

In an Instagram tribute, she noted that it had been 24 years — ironically, the same number Bryant wore for the Lakers — since they first crossed paths in the Palisades when they were "both young and ambitious."

articles.title: Nana Patekar passes away at 75: Actor's last rites to be held at his Pune farmhouse
articles.summary: Bollywood mourns the loss of veteran actor Nana Patekar, renowned for his powerful performances and contributions to Indian cinema, as he passes away at the age of 75.
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar has passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest. The National Award-winning actor was among the most respected and distinctive performers in Hindi and Marathi cinema.Nana Patekar was found unconscious at his Goa homeThe actor was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was subsequently rushed to a hospital, but the doctors declared him dead. According to ANI, Dr. Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department, Manipal Hospital, has shared that despite 45 minutes of continuous CPR, the actor could not be revived. Further, a medico-legal case (MLC) has been registered, and a post-mortem is being conducted.GMC Dean JP Tiwari has constituted a team of three doctors for the autopsy. This panel includes Dr Kedar Narvekar, Associate Professor, Department of Medicine, Dr Pannag S Kumar, Assistant Professor, Department of Forensic Medicine and Dr Peter Rodrigues, Lecturer, Department of Pathology.Nana Patekar's last rites to be held at his Pune farmhouseAccording to PTI, the last rites of Nana Patekar will be performed at his farmhouse, located at Donje on the outskirts of Pune, Maharashtra, on Thursday."The mortal remains will be brought (to Pune) by around 5 pm, and later will be kept for the last 'darshan'. The last rites will be performed on the premises of his farmhouse," said Ganesh Thorat, the CEO of the actor's Naam Foundation.Further, Maharashtra Culture Minister Ashish Shelar has shared that Nana Patekar will be accorded a state funeral. The decision has been taken by the Devendra Fadnavis government, considering the late legendary's artist's unparalleled contribution to Marathi theatre and Marathi as well as Hindi cinema.Film industry pays tribute to Nana PatekarThe news has shattered the industry, with the film fraternity members and fans trying to process the loss. After the news of Nana Patekar's demise came out, Marathi actor Siddharth Jadhav expressed his grief. While speaking to ETimes, he said he is " in shock after knowing about the death; this was not the time to go. He had many things to do yet. In deep shock, couldn't process the news."Meanwhile, several actors have taken to their social media handles to express their profound grief. “I was deeply saddened to hear the extremely tragic news of Nana Patekar Ji’s passing early this morning. Despite being a star, Nana Ji was always far removed from the trappings of stardom,” shared Ravi Kishan on his social media story.He recalled the late actor as “one of the great artists of Indian cinema, known for his simplicity, humility and his down-to-earth personality.”“Even while living amidst the glitz and glamour of Mumbai, he never lost touch with his roots and values. I shared a close and warm relationship with Nana Ji. We would speak from time to time, and I learned a great deal from his acting, simplicity and perspective on life,” wrote the actor-politician.About Nana PatekarBorn as Vishwanath Patekar in 1951 in Maharashtra, Nana Patekar’s journey into the world of acting started in the late 1970s. 'Gaman' was his debut film; following it, he gave one performance after another to establish himself in the industry.Some of his most loved cinematic pieces include 'Parinda', 'Prahaar', 'Angaar', 'Krantiveer', 'Agni Sakshi', 'Yashwant', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', 'Apaharan', 'Welcome' and 'Natsamrat', among several others. His performances frequently moved beyond conventional hero and villain roles.The late legendary star was honoured with the National Award thrice. In 1989, he received the National Award for Best Supporting Actor for 'Parinda' and got the Best Actor title for 'Krantiveer in 1994. Then in 1996, he was again honoured with the National Award for Best Supporting Actor in 'Agni Sakshi.' Further, he was honoured with the Padma Shri for his contribution to the arts in 2013.Nana Patekar built a career spanning several decades across films, theatre and television. With powerful screen presence, intense dialogue delivery and the ability to portray complex characters with remarkable restraint, the actor made a unique place for himself in Indian cinema.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Nana Patekar’s sudden demise has left the film industry in deep shock and sorrow. The veteran actor, who was 75, passed away on Thursday morning, October 8, after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was found unconscious and was rushed to a hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him for around 45 minutes. However, he could not be saved and was declared dead at around 5:20 am.Known for his intense performances and powerful screen presence, Nana Patekar leaves behind a rich body of work spanning Hindi and Marathi cinema. Among his most celebrated performances was his titular role in 'Krantiveer,' which earned him the National Film Award for Best Actor. His work in films such as 'Parinda,' 'Agni Sakshi,' 'Ab Tak Chhappan,' 'Natsamrat,' and 'Welcome' further established his versatility as an actor.For many, 'Krantiveer' remains one of Nana Patekar’s most iconic films, with his powerful performance and memorable moments continuing to resonate with audiences. His work in the film also takes fans back to the popular song 'Love Rap,' which featured Nana alongside the cast.ETimes contacted actor-producer Atul Agnihotri, who had the opportunity to work with Nana Patekar in 'Krantiveer' and 'Yeshwant.' Recalling his association with the late actor, Atul said, "I am deeply saddened and shocked by the sudden passing of Nana ji.I had the privilege of working with him in 'Krantiveer' and 'Yeshwant,' and those memories will always hold a very special place in my heart. Working with Nana ji was an experience in itself. His intensity, honesty, and complete commitment to his craft were extraordinary. He had an aura and presence that were impossible to ignore, both on screen and off it."Atul also expressed his condolences to Nana Patekar’s family. He said, "My deepest condolences to Malhar and the entire Patekar family. articles.title: Meet Nana Patekar’s wife Neelakanti Patekar, the award-winning actor who gave up IIT for the arts
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, a towering presence in Hindi and Marathi cinema, breathed his last at the age of 75.
articles.body: Nana Patekar, a towering presence in Hindi and Marathi cinema, breathed his last at the age of 75. The actor suffered a cardiac arrest at his Goa home and passed away at 5:20 am on Thursday, as confirmed by Dr Shekhar Salkar, head of Oncology at Manipal Hospital, in a statement to ANI. His wife, Neelakanti, who has had her own career in Marathi theatre and films, and their son, Malhar, survive him.How Neelakanti Patekar and Nana Patekar's love story beganThe love story of Nana Patekar and Neelakanti began on the Marathi stage. Neelakanti, then a bank officer who pursued acting alongside her job, became a friend before she became his partner. They married in 1978. Their early married life was marked by joy as well as grief, as they lost their first child at the age of two and a half.Neelakanti Patekar's unconventional path to actingNeelakanti took an unusual road to acting. She was born in Pune, but her father's postings in the Central Excise Department meant she spent her childhood in several different cities. She went on to study Physics, and when her father pushed her to try the IIT entrance exam, she passed it. But theatre was what she really wanted, so she chose the stage over an engineering career.Neelakanti Patekar's award-winning career in theatre and cinemaDespite her background in Physics, Neelakanti's heart was in acting. She became deeply involved in Marathi theatre and earned a name for herself as a performer, winning the Gold Medal for Best Actress at the Maharashtra State Drama Competition in 1973. She later moved into Marathi cinema, and in 1989 she starred opposite Sachin Pilgaonkar in Aatm Vishwas, a film he also directed. Her performance in the lead role earned her the Maharashtra State Government's Best Actress award.Neelakanti Patekar's comeback with ‘Chhaava’Neelakanti returned to acting after a long break from the limelight. She appeared in the historical drama ‘Chhaava’, starring Vicky Kaushal and Rashmika Mandanna, in the role of Dharau.Neelakanti Patekar and Nana Patekar: married but living apartNana and Neelakanti never divorced, but over time they chose to live apart. In an earlier interview reported by Indian Express, Nana reflected on their relationship, saying, "Nilkanti and I shared numerous years of happiness together. We supported each other through thick and thin. But, over the years, we developed certain irreconcilable differences and grew apart. Today, we continue to be married but stay separately."Neelakanti Patekar and the loss of their first sonThe couple's journey included a deep personal grief, the death of their first son. articles.title: Nana Patekar's mortal remains sent for postmortem doctor confirms; reveals details of actor's final moments before death - WATCH
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar, one of the country's most notable stars, passed away at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday morning, at age 75.
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar, one of the country's most notable stars, passed away at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday morning, at age 75.An official confirmation from the Manipal Hospital, Goa, stated that the actor was found unconscious at his Dona Paula, residence and was rushed to the hospital.In a video statement to the media, Dr Shekhar Salkar shared the details about the actor's final moments. Recalling the events of the night, Dr Salkar shared, "Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital, somewhere around 4.30 am and was declared dead by 5.30 am. We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45 minutes to 1 hour, but he just could not be saved."Reconstructing the timeline of events from the early hours of thursday morning, the doctor said, "Somewhere around 2.30 am, he sent a message to his friend that he was not feeling well. But as it was night, he could not see the message. He went to his house at around 4 am. At that time, he was sweating. He was slowly becoming unconscious, so they sent his caretaker because they stay near the hospital."The doctor also revealed that it was the actor's caretaker and friends who rushed him to the hospital, he shared that "His family was not there."The doctor added, "The caretaker came to the hospital, took our ambulance and went with our ER team. They started cardiac massage and shifted him to the hospital somewhere around 4.20 am or 4.30 am. We also tried here to our maximum, but he was brought dead."He also confirmed that a formal police case has been registered and confirmed, "The body has now been taken to the morgue in Goa Medical College for postmortem."In a statement to PTI, he shared that investigation into the cause of death is on. He said, "It was a cardiac arrest, but we do not know the cause. He was a known cardiac patient and was on medication, as far as we have been told."Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced that Nana Patekar would be accorded a state funeral in recognition of his immense contribution to Indian cinema. In a post on X, Ashish Shelar wrote, "Considering the unparalleled contribution of actor Nana Patekar to Marathi plays as well as Marathi and Hindi cinema, we have decided to conduct his last rites 'with full state honors'."He also spoke to the media and expressed his grief over the actor's demise. "The departure of Nana Patekar ji is a profound loss for the world of art. Emerging from the lanes of Yeola, he carved out his identity in Marathi theatre, Marathi and Hindi cinema through the strength of his talent and perseverance. On his passing, heartfelt condolences from me, from the Government of Maharashtra, and from the Department of Cultural Affairs," he said.See More: Nana Patekar passes away: PM Modi hails veteran star's contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinemaGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sarah Santaolalla, tras la muerte de Maricarmen: "No olvidaremos, no perdonaremos"
articles.standfirst: La analista política se pronuncia en sus redes sociales
articles.summary: La analista política se pronuncia en sus redes sociales
articles.body: Sarah Santaolalla, analista política y tertuliana habitual, se ha pronunciado sobre la muerte de Maricarmen y ha criticado a los sectores y personas que, según su criterio, han provocado el fallecimiento de esta anciana de 87 años. "Maricarmen acaba de fallecer. Los fondos buitres, los rentistas y los miserables políticos y mediáticos han acabado con la vida de Maricarmen", ha afirmado. "No olvidaremos, no perdonaremos", ha insistido en su cuenta personal de X, antes Twitter. Maricarmen fue desahuciada a los 87 años, provocando un aluvión de reacciones y movilizaciones sociales en todo el país. Su nombre, que aparece hasta en el decreto ley sobre la vivienda publicado en el Boletín Oficial del Estado, se ha convertido en una figura clave en el debate la sobre la vivienda en España. Tras su muerte, el miércoles por la noche, las reacciones de la clase política y los medios de comunicación han sido constantes. Sarah Santaolalla ha insistido en sus críticas en las redes sociales a las personas que, según ella, han colaborado para que perdiera la vida. "Todos los que habéis contribuido al asesinato de Maricarmen sois basura. Desde políticos de la derecha, programas llenos de miserables, periodistas desalmados y caseros podridos de dinero, no tenéis perdón. Sois lo peor que le ha pasado a este país", ha publicado la tertuliana. La analista política, muy activa en redes en estas últimas horas, ha compartido en X algunos mensajes sobre Maricarmen de medios de comunicación y políticos. "Lista de indeseables", ha escrito Sarah Santaolalla mientras repasaba algunas publicaciones recientes en Twitter, artículos en prensa e intervenciones televisivas. Son muchos los que consideran a Maricarmen como un símbolo de la lucha por la vivienda en España y, de hecho, su nombre llega a aparecer en el decreto ley, reflejado en el Boletín Oficial del Estado.

articles.title: Acclaimed Indian actor Nana Patekar dies aged 75
articles.summary: Patekar won three National Film Awards and received the Padma Shri, one of the country’s highest civilian honours.
articles.body:
Nana Patekar, an acclaimed Indian actor and filmmaker known for his ⁠fiery performances ⁠in Bollywood films and theatre, has died aged 75.

Patekar died of a suspected cardiac arrest at his home in Goa, the Press Trust of India news agency reported on Thursday, quoting a doctor at the hospital where he was pronounced dead.

His son, Malhar Patekar, confirmed his death, saying the actor died of natural causes. A medico-legal case was registered, and a post-mortem examination will be conducted, officials said.

Patekar’s career spanned nearly five decades across Hindi and Marathi cinema, theater and filmmaking.

Born in 1951 in India’s western state of Maharashtra, Patekar built a career spanning nearly five decades in Hindi- and Marathi-language cinema. He was known for intense performances and roles that often portrayed complex or unconventional characters.

Patekar made his film debut in the 1978 Hindi film Gaman, and later earned acclaim for Parinda and Krantiveer. He gained wider international recognition with filmmaker Mira Nair’s Oscar-nominated Salaam Bombay!

He won three National Film Awards, India’s highest film honours, and received the Padma Shri, one of the country’s highest civilian honours.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi mourned Patekar’s death, praising his “intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence” as an actor.

“He brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and gave us characters that will be remembered for generations,” Modi wrote on X.

He played a variety of roles, sharing screen space with actors such as Amitabh Bachchan and Shah Rukh Khan ⁠and excelling in both serious and comic roles.

“He was one of those rare actors who never needed to do too much to make you sit up and watch. ‌That voice, that intensity, that honesty in every performance… he was completely his own,” said actor Akshay Kumar, who starred with ‌Patekar ‌in several movies.

In 2018, as the #MeToo movement swept the world, Patekar was accused by an Indian actress of sexual harassment during the making of a film in 2008. He denied the allegation and a court in Mumbai dismissed the case last year.

Patekar’s death came days after he appeared at a theater event in Goa, where he spoke about the importance of keeping the performing arts alive.

Patekar is survived by his wife, from whom he was separated, and a son.

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s wife financially supported him when he earned Rs 50 per show, actor once recalled traumatic time of elder son’s death at 2: ‘I used to smoke 60 cigarettes a day’
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, who died at 75 in Goa on Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest, is survived by his wife Neelkanthi and son Malhar.
articles.body: Nana Patekar, who died at 75 in Goa on Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest, is survived by his wife Neelkanthi and son Malhar. While Nana and Neelkanthi spent much of their married life living separately, the two remained married and never divorced. Their relationship also endured one of the most painful tragedies a parent can face — the death of their elder son Durvasa, who passed away at just two-and-a-half years of age.Nana had spoken candidly about his marriage, family and the losses that shaped him in an earlier conversation with The Lallantop. Recalling how he first met Neelkanthi, the actor said the two worked together in the play ‘Jaat Na Pucho Sadhu Ki’. While Nana was trying to establish himself as an actor, Neelkanthi was also working as a bank officer and was earning considerably more than him at the time.“She was working as an officer in a bank. I would get paid Rs 50 per show, and she had a salary of Rs 2500. I could only make Rs 750 after doing 15-20 shows,” he recalled.Nana said Neelkanthi’s financial and emotional support gave him the freedom to pursue acting at a time when there was no guarantee that it would work out. “She told me that if you want to pursue this as a career… I am already making money so we have money coming in for the family. I am very grateful to her. I could pursue this profession only because of her. We didn’t know at that time if I would be successful or not,” he said.Eventually, Neelkanthi stepped away from acting to look after the family. Around the same period, the couple began living separately. Neelkanthi stayed with Nana’s mother and their son Malhar, while Nana lived separately.Nana also spoke openly about the devastating loss of his elder son Durvasa. He revealed that the child was born with a cleft palate and had difficulty seeing through one eye. The actor admitted that his initial reaction was driven by concern about how others would perceive him rather than what his child was going through.See More: National Award winnig actor Nana Patekar passes away at 75“My elder son was born with a cleft palate. He also had difficulty seeing through one eye. The first thought that ran through my mind when I’d see him like this was, ‘What will people think about me, that my son looks like this’. Imagine what a terrible man I am. My first worry was what people would say about me, not him,” he said.Durvasa, whom Nana said he had named after the ‘angriest rishi’, died when he was only two-and-a-half. Looking back at the tragedy, Nana said the child had a profound impact on his life despite his short time with the family.“He died at the age of two-and-a-half, but he taught me so much. He’s the triggering point. It happens…” he said.The actor also recalled how he dealt with the grief in the aftermath of his son’s death, saying that he never allowed himself to remain consumed by it. “I’ve always had a chin-up attitude. I don’t cry. I cry only in the movies, and I do that for money,” he said.However, Nana admitted that the loss affected him deeply and pushed him towards excessive smoking. He revealed that there was a period when he smoked around 60 cigarettes a day and even smoked while taking a shower.“At that time, I used to smoke about 60 cigarettes a day. I even smoked while bathing. But it’s a very bad thing. No one would sit in my car because of the foul smell. I never drank alcohol much but I smoked a lot,” he recalled.Nana Patekar died after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. His son Malhar confirmed the news to The Indian Express and said, “Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with a detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons.”See More: Nana Patekar passes away: PM Modi hails veteran star's contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinemaGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Aitana despide el verano con un posado desde una playa paradisiaca
articles.standfirst: La cantante se resiste a decir adiós a la época estival
articles.summary: La cantante se resiste a decir adiós a la época estival
articles.body: Es muy común que las celebridades muestren en sus redes sociales su día a día. Influencers, futbolistas o cantantes, entre otros, viajan durante el verano a los mejores destinos del mundo para disfrutar de los mayores placeres de la vida: el sol, la playa y un agua cristalina en la que refrescarse de vez en cuando. Para ello, son numerosos los destinos a los que viajar, destacando la Costa Brava o Islas Baleares en cuanto al territorio nacional se refiere. Pero, sin duda, una de las mejores opciones fuera de España son Bali o las Maldivas. Aitana Ocaña se ha convertido en una de las artistas más mediáticas de España. La cantante llena cada uno de los estadios en los que pone en marcha uno de sus conciertos y se muestra muy feliz e ilusionada siempre con su pareja, el youtuber Plex. Precisamente, ha sido la cantante catalana la que todavía no ha querido despedir el verano, o es lo que muestra en sus redes sociales, con fotos de un viaje en el que no ha confirmado si es actual o pasado. Aun así, se le puede ver disfrutando de una playa paradisiaca. Se desconoce si el autor de las fotos es Plex, pero en ellas puede verse a la cantante en tres de las cuatro imágenes, con diferentes posados. En una de ellas, viste un vestido estilo pareo con transparencias, foto que posteriormente repite, pero solo con la prenda de ropa pendiendo de una rama de un árbol. En las otras dos imágenes, se puede ver a una Aitana con la parte superior de un bikini blanco despojada mirando a la cámara y, en la última de las imágenes del carrusel, viste un bikini de color marrón con topos amarillos y se encuentra de espaldas a la cámara. De esta manera, Aitana demuestra a todos sus seguidores un merecido descanso después de un verano de mucho trabajo en el que ha llegado a realizar un total de 13 apariciones entre conciertos y colaboraciones. Además, cabe destacar que la cantante está a las puertas de reanudar la gira por Latinoamérica, que comienza el 16 de octubre.

articles.title: Mia Goth files for divorce from Shia LaBeouf after nearly 10 year marriage
articles.summary: Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf nearly 10 years after the two actors were married.
articles.body: Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf nearly 10 years after the two actors were married. The petition filed Tuesday in Los Angeles County Superior Court says the 32-year-old Goth and the 40-year-old LaBeouf have been separated since July 2025. The two met and became a couple while filming “Nymphomaniac: Vol. II” in 2012, and married in 2016. They had previously split and said they were divorcing in 2018, but remained legally married, reunited in 2020 and had a daughter in 2022. Goth is seeking primary legal and physical custody of the 4-year-old, with visitation rights for LaBeouf. She also asked the court to deny either party spousal support. It was the first marriage for both. As with most U.S. divorces, irreconcilable differences were cited as the reason for the split. Representatives for Goth and LaBeouf did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment. The actor, born Mia Gypsy Mello da Silva Goth in London, most recently appeared as the unfaithful servant Melantho in this summer’s “The Odyssey,” and had a dual role in last year’s “Frankenstein.” She previously starred in the horror trilogy “X,” “Pearl” and “MaXXXine.” LaBeouf was a child star on the Disney Channel’s “Even Stevens” and in the 2003 film “Holes.” He later starred in “Indiana Jones and the Crystal Skull” and director Michael Bay’s first three “Transformers” films. The day before Goth filed for divorce, LaBeouf, for the second time, settled a lawsuit with singer, songwriter and actor FKA Twigs, whom he dated when he was split from Goth. FKA Twigs, whose legal name is Tahliah Barnett, had alleged in a suit filed in 2020 that LaBeouf emotionally and physically abused her during their relationship that began when she had a supporting role in the semi-autobiographical film “Honey Boy,” which he wrote and starred in. The two settled the lawsuit and had it dismissed last year, but she sued him again in March, saying nondisclosure provisions in the settlement illegally silenced her under California law. On Monday, she moved to dismiss the second lawsuit, saying in court documents that LaBeouf had agreed to void those provisions. In June, LaBeouf was sentenced to probation after pleading guilty to punching three people outside a New Orleans bar during Mardi Gras.

articles.title: Cupertino might be made for your mom, but it’s a good take on tech
articles.summary: The Social Reckoning has been outsmarted by a new CBS procedural.
articles.body: Cupertino brings the tech backlash to the CBS procedural — an initially awkward combination, but with rewarding results. The show starts off just slightly unsure, but quickly figures out what to do with these strange times, creating fictionalized dupes of the Zizians, Polymarket, Jeff Bezos’ looksmaxxing obsession, OpenAI stealing Scarlett Johansson’s voice, and the fight for AI guardrails, among other familiar tales, and using them to speak to the feeling of helplessness in the face of rapid change that extends well beyond the greater San Francisco area. It turns out the seemingly outdated tools of broadcast TV are a fantastic way to tackle our uncertain future. Please don’t think Cupertino is some kind of Blue Bloods Bay Area or CSI: The Computer. (Sorry, I mean CSI: Cyber, a real show that lasted two seasons and starred Ted Danson, obviously.) Yes, the show is network TV, in the old-fashioned, 20-episodes-in-a-season sense, and it’s airing on CBS in the highly suspicious age of Ellison. But it has certain pedigree coming from creators Robert and Michelle King, the married couple behind the wonderful Elsbeth, Evil, The Good Wife, and The Good Fight. The Kings are often credited as uniquely sophisticated for network TV. But that still leaves some big questions about what this show is and who it’s for. Also, yes, it is (mostly) a case-of-the-week show about an upstart Silicon Valley law firm taking on Big Tech one suit at a time. Price Siffre (pronounced “cipher”) is made up of lawyers Michael Price (Mike Colter, aka Luke Cage) and Olivia Siffre (Rachel Keller, Legion), along with their assistant Christy Palladino (Ella Stiller), all of whom left the same evil AI company under not-great circumstances in the pilot. (My recommendation is to skip that first episode — just know they sue tech companies — or at least don’t hold it against the show.) Cipher maybe isn’t the wrong word for this main group: Michael is handsome and guarded, Christy is a King-classic spunky investigator type, and Olivia is religious and loves musicals, so she’s introduced listening to Godspell — it took me probably four whole episodes to forgive the show for that too-cute detail. The ensemble really starts to come together, though, when it’s revealed to be a secret Girls5eva reunion, with the additions of Renée Elise Goldsberry as Michael’s ex/rival and Busy Philipps as MacKenzie Scott (formerly Bezos) if she was very fun and a little drunk. Maybe that’s not quite selling you — two out of five members of a fake girl group from a criminally underwatched sitcom and a bunch of ripped-from-the-headlines tech trials, made by people in their 60s for people in their 60s. But the Kings have their bona fides when it comes to the subject matter — The Good Wife was called “the most tech-savvy show on TV” by Wired in 2013, the same year that BuzzFeed said “everyone in tech needs to be watching” it. That show tackled Bitcoin, viral videos, NSA spying, and the goofy-ass names of 2010s tech startups without being hacky or hammy. Granted, being “good at tech” on an Obama-era show about lawyers in Chicago is different from being “good at tech” on a 2026 show called Cupertino. [Image: Olivia Siffre (Rachel Keller) and Michael Price (Mike Colter) are as surprised as anyone that they’re founding law firm to take on Big Tech. One of the creators’ greatest strengths is worldbuilding, and as their vision of Silicon Valley expands it starts to cohere. This is a landscape packed with data brokers, rationalists, underpaid AI trainers, software developers who put ASCII dicks in their code as a gag, gerontocratic judges, petty billionaires, and the frustrated contractors who build their offices and bunkers. That’s where a perceived weakness becomes a strength: The longer network season allows for tangents, explorations, multi-episode arcs, successful fake-outs, and surprise recurrences. These figures can, do, and likely will return, and the show has the time and space to let them unfold and disappear until their resurfacing is a delight. It’s a trick rarely so surprising or fun in clockwork six-to-13-episode streaming seasons, when a detail in episode 3 pretty much has to pay off in episode 7. This isn’t just good TV, it creates a sense of truth and claustrophobia that the show benefits from; these well-drawn people (mostly) all feel caught together in a highly specific and completely deranging reality. So it follows that the prevailing mood is sort of a peppy paranoia — the dark twist of actual reality, though, is that we’re post-paranoid. Suspicion about the reaches and aims of Big Tech has been shown to be grounded and, frankly, reasonable. The firm’s work suing “the big seven” fictionalized companies comes at a time when every device could be listening and deepfakes mean nothing’s guaranteed to be what it seems. Who wouldn’t be looking over their shoulder, under their desk, and into the source code? Somehow still, though, the show approaches its central preoccupation — AI — with a healthy fear but surprising lack of judgment. This can be frustrating if you’re sensitive about bots being anthropomorphized (oh, that’s happening, all right), and there were moments early on when I feared the “wrong” lessons were being imparted. But the lack of clean or easy answers makes this a subtler take on what we should be scared of today. Cupertino arrives at a time when tech backlash is coming to screens in a big, big way — in cinemas with The Social Reckoning, You Can See Everything, Artificial, and Musk, and on TV too with The Altruists, a Netflix show about FTX coming in November, and AMC’s The Audacity hitting Netflix this past summer. But while The Audacity felt like it was preaching to (and occasionally screaming at) the choir, Cupertino’s key is that it’s about to be fed to an audience that might not be following the finer points of the Hugging Face hack, and riffing on these themes, stories, and real-life archetypes with intelligence, nuance, and some small remainder of joy.

articles.summary: El exfutbolista confiesa su enorme ilusión por esta nueva etapa profesional
articles.body: Mario Suárez es el nuevo fichaje de Movistar Plus para 'La Casa del Fútbol'. El exfutbolista de Atlético de Madrid, con el que logró seis títulos, Celta de Vigo, Valladolid, Fiorentina, Watford, Valencia y Rayo Vallecano se encargará de comentar la Liga de Campeones y también participará en 'Deporte Plus'. De hecho, se estrenará en este espacio el próximo domingo 11 de octubre. Mario Suárez no ha escondido la ilusión por afrontar este nuevo proyecto profesional: "En esta nueva etapa de mi vida, incorporarme a Movistar Plus creo que es el paso que me tocaba dar. Estoy supermotivado, con ganas de poder comentar la mejor competición del mundo, participar en programas y deseando que empiece ya". El exjugador, además, ha confesado cuáles son sus programas favoritos. "Cuando pienso en Movistar Plus, siempre lo primero que se me viene a la cabeza son los mejores partidos, 'El Día Después' y su sección 'Lo que el ojo no ve'. Ya de pequeño veía 'El Día Después'. 'Lo que el ojo no ve' me encantaba y me sigue encantando", ha explicado. El exfutbolista ha reconocido que disfruta más en el campo, pero ha insistido en la motivación de estar en el otro bando. Me hace mucha ilusión poder trabajar con Carlos Martínez, con Maldini y con todos los profesionales de esta casa", ha comentado. Mario Suárez, que acumula un gran conocimiento del fútbol tras su extensa y exitosa carrera profesional, ha desvelado cuál sería su retransmisión soñada con Movistar Plus. "Me encantaría comentar la final de Champions, que se disputa en el Metropolitano esta temporada, con el Atlético de Madrid, y que gane el Atlético de Madrid", ha dejado claro.

articles.title: Wynonna Judd admits helping daughter during meth battle ‘bit me in the butt'
articles.summary: Wynonna Judd reveals she enabled Grace Kelley's meth addiction by giving her money for drugs, a painful realization explored on her album "The Hard Truth."
articles.body: Wynonna Judd is reflecting on the painful lesson she learned while trying to help her daughter Grace Kelley through her years-long battle with methamphetamine addiction. Kelley, 30, has struggled with drug addiction and faced a string of related legal troubles for more than a decade. She is currently serving a 15-month sentence at Rockingham County Jail in Harrisonburg, Virginia, after pleading guilty in June to a felony charge of driving with a suspended or revoked license. During an interview with Fox News Digital, Judd, 62, who recently released her deeply personal album "The Hard Truth," candidly opened up about coming to the realization that some of her attempts to help Kelley only exacerbated her daughter's problems. CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT "I really lost myself with Grace and I enabled her, which comes down to basically giving her money for drugs," Judd admitted. "And here I thought I was buying her a car. And those things really bit me in the butt." "And I'm still feeling, you know, some guilt and shame about that," she added. LADY A'S CHARLES KELLEY SHARES BEFORE-AND-AFTER PHOTOS SHOWING HOW SOBRIETY TRANSFORMED HIS LIFE The country star also shared what she would tell other parents struggling to help their children without enabling them. "I would say work on yourself," Judd said. "That was one of the things that I was told. And working on myself, getting the peace, letting her see that she's attracted to that. Maybe she wants to get better herself. So let the light shine." COUNTRY HITMAKER REVEALS HOW FAITH CARRIED HIM THROUGH SON'S MURDER — AND TOWARD COMPASSION FOR HIS KILLER "Let your light shine through the cracks, that's how they see the light," she continued. "And hopefully she'll want the same thing that I have. Find someone whose recovery you love so much that you want to be like them and go and do it." "The Hard Truth" is Judd's first solo studio album in more than a decade as well as her first time serving as a primary songwriter. The album explores heartbreak, healing, faith and survival while shining a light on some of the most painful chapters of Judd's life, including her complicated relationship with her late mother Naomi Judd and Kelley's struggles. WATCH: WYNONNA JUDD SAYS HELPING DAUGHTER THROUGH METH BATTLE ‘BIT ME IN THE BUTT’ HAYDEN PANETTIERE DEFENDS GIVING UP CUSTODY OF HER DAUGHTER DESPITE INTENSE 'EMOTIONAL PAIN' While speaking with Fox News Digital, Judd opened up about the hardest truth that she had to face while making the album. "That there might be a chance that my daughter doesn't get clean, that she doesn't find the healing that she so desperately needs," Judd admitted. "As a mother, I'm devastated by her story, and I just had to let go." ‘NO CONTACT’ ON THE RISE: NEARLY 2 IN 5 AMERICANS CUT TIES WITH LOVED ONES The six-time Grammy Award winner also reflected on her current estrangement from Kelley, with whom she said she has not spoken for a year. "After all these years, the money ran out, and she did, too," Judd said. "And I just have to make peace with the fact that I did everything I could do. Including enabling, and I've had to deal with that. And just the pain of losing her to meth and realizing that there's absolutely nothing I can do to save her anymore." 'BAYWATCH: HAWAII' STAR BRANDY LEDFORD SAYS SHE 'WANTED TO TRULY CHECK OUT' BEFORE REHAB SAVED HER LIFE Judd explained that her last conversation with Kelley was difficult since she had stood by her decision to stop enabling her daughter. "Things were tense because I wasn't giving her money anymore and helping her to go back to rehab again and again and again, and again," Judd said. "And I just had to say, 'Sweetheart, you know, you're 30 years old. It's time to stop blaming your mom. And I want you to get the help that you need, and you're gonna have to do it yourself.'" COUNTRY SINGER RUSTON KELLY COMMITS TO SOBRIETY AFTER RELAPSING ON DRUGS FOLLOWING FREAK GOLF CART CRASH Judd told Fox News Digital that while she still has hope for a reconciliation with Kelley, there is one condition that would have to come first before they could begin rebuilding their relationship. "Sobriety," she said. "You are not supposed to make any major decisions in your life, including relationships for a year after you get clean and sober. And I would ask her to go to rehab again, because I know that that's what worked for me." CARA DELEVINGNE ADMITS SHE USED PARTY DRUG GHB DAILY BEFORE TERRIFYING SEIZURES FORCED HER SOBER In 2006, Judd checked herself into the Shades of Hope Center of Headling in Buffalo Gap, Texas, where she underwent a 42-day treatment program to address her struggles with food addiction. She told Fox News Digital that her own time in treatment shaped the way she views recovery and the example she wants to set for Kelley. "I'm gonna express that to her, of course, and you're not supposed to really go there. You want the person to want it themselves," Judd said. "But it would take some time because we've been apart a lot. She's been homeless and struggling for years and in and out of prison." "And I have a song on the record called ‘Drive,’ which talks about me driving down to see her in prison back when she was incarcerated," she continued. "And I'm just gonna look forward to that day. I still have hope she's alive. There is still hope." Judd shares Kelley and son Elijah, 31, with her first husband Arch Kelley III, to whom she was married from 1996 to 1998. During a recent appearance on the "Shawn Ryan Show," Judd reflected on how her demanding career may have affected Grace differently than it did Elijah. "Grace was very jealous of my career because it took me away from her enough to where she was not satisfied," she said. "I think because she's the second born, I think it was important to her that I even spend more time with her because I had that with Elijah for a minute." "He was more at peace about it," Judd continued. "She was the one that wanted to sleep with me, wanted my attention 24/7." "So that was painful. That was hard. I was really hard on myself about that," she admitted. Judd also spoke candidly about the toll of her daughter’s addiction, describing herself as "a mom in waiting." "I'm waiting for my daughter to return from a nightmarish addiction to meth," she said. "And it has been quite a journey." "And unfortunately, she's been incarcerated since … on and off since she was 17," she continued. "I've made all the jokes about, 'I have one on parole. I have one on patrol,'" Judd added. "My son is a deputy. I've done all that, and now it's time to just tell my story as a mom who's constantly in this place between hell and hallelujah." Judd said setting boundaries with Kelley became one of the hardest decisions of her life, recalling how she struggled with refusing to help her daughter even when she reached out in desperation. "I had to let go, and that means no more enabling," she explained. "And it about killed me because when your kid calls and says, 'I'm hungry,' what do you do?" The "No One Else on Earth" singer said Kelley’s repeated incarceration and the dangers surrounding drug use made her realize that enabling her daughter could have life-or-death consequences. "She's been in and out of prison and jail for so long that that's her way of walking through the addiction part in terms of what it costs her," Judd said. "We're also now dealing with fentanyl. So, there's that." "I realized, 'Oh my God, it's possible that I could be part of the reason she dies. I'm loving her to death. Literally,'" she shared. Judd said she believes that Kelley still carries resentment over the time her career took away from their relationship, as well as her decision to step in and raise her granddaughter Kaliyah. "Grace is really mad at me right now," she said. "Because I had a career, and I was busy, and she didn't have enough of me in the beginning. I did the best I could. I've made a lot of mistakes, and she's really mad at me for stepping in with her child." "Kaliyah has Type 1 diabetes," Judd continued. "There's no way she could have taken care of her. That's one thing. It's a 24/7 situation. I stepped in, and I took over, and she's mad at me." "I understand that that's her journey," she added. "It's not mine. My journey is to raise this baby to be the healthiest and break the cycle." Judd and her third husband, musician Cactus Moser, who she married in 2012, have been the primary caregivers for Kaliyah, 4, since her infancy and legally adopted her amid Kelley's addiction struggles and legal woes. The singer was previously married to former bodyguard D.R. Roach from 2003 until 2007. Moser and Judd are currently raising Kaliyah on their 500-acre farm in Tennessee. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Wynonna (@wynonnajudd) When asked by Fox News Digital about how she balances protecting Kaliyah while leaving the door open for Kelley to be part of her life someday, Judd said her focus remains on giving her granddaughter a grounded childhood. "I haven't answered that yet," she said. "I think I'm still in the part where I'm so hell-bent on keeping her out of the iPad and the phone and TV. We live on a farm, and she mucks stalls and does chores and she's a cowgirl. So I'm so centered on that. I haven't really given that a lot of thought and if and when that happens I'll answer your question." Judd also shared a glimpse into her day-to-day life on the farm with Kaliyah and Moser. "Getting away with as much as possible without having to do anything, going on a side by side, ride down to the lake, taking her fishing, we do that a lot," she told Fox News Digital. "And being out in the woods, just being outside is just so heavenly." Judd described their farm as a "peace place," noting that her life at home is much simpler than her life onstage. "I'm known in our family as the cook, and I'm known as Nonie," Judd continued. "When I don't have on my lashes, I am known as Nonie." During her appearance on the "Shawn Ryan Show," Judd said she learned about the baby through social media and knows little about the child’s circumstances. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo calls women-focused festival ‘one hundred percent’ political, tells critics to not buy a ticket
articles.summary: Olivia Rodrigo confirmed Daisy Chain Fields was "one hundred percent" political, raising $20 million for Planned Parenthood and other charities.
articles.body: Grammy-winning singer Olivia Rodrigo said her women-focused music festival Daisy Chain Fields was "one hundred percent" political, saying critics who disagree with her message "don’t have to buy a ticket." Headlined by Rodrigo, the one-day music festival in Irvine, Calif., featured an all-female lineup including performances by Chappell Roan, Sarah McLachlan and Stevie Nicks. Net proceeds from Daisy Chain Fields were directed toward nonprofit organizations "dedicated to advancing and advocating for women and girls," including Planned Parenthood, the Center for Reproductive Rights, Baby2Baby and the Black Mamas Matter Alliance. The festival raised $20 million for the women-focused charities and Rodrigo made it clear that she planned the festival with politics in mind. PLANNED PARENTHOOD ACROSS MIDWEST AT RISK DUE TO LACK OF FEDERAL FUNDS AFTER 3 FACILITIES CLOSE IN MICHIGAN "One hundred percent, yes," she told The Hollywood Reporter when asked whether Daisy Chain Fields was political. "But I think it’s also about joy," she added. "I think the two things can exist at the same time, they kind of have to … I think young people have lost hope in our leaders and lost hope in each other. I really wanted to galvanize people and be evidence of what can happen when you come together and are part of something and contribute." The "Drivers License" singer also stated that those who don't agree with the festival's political message don't have to buy a ticket. "Everyone is welcome to come to Daisy Chain. But if you don’t agree with the message that we’re sending, then you don’t have to buy a ticket," she said. ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS Daisy Chain Fields was inspired by Lilith Fair, an all-female traveling music festival launched in the late 1990s by McLachlan, who was frustrated over the lack of female representation in the music industry. Rodrigo, 23, argued that women had more rights in the 1990s than they do in 2026. "When Lilith Fair was happening 30 years ago, women in America had more rights, had more autonomy over their bodies," the singer said. "I’ve always felt really protective of my young fans, and when I play a show and I look out into the audience and see young girls with their friends or their moms or their families, I feel such a kinship with them," she continued. "And if I could be a small part in making the world a safer and better place for them to grow up and live, that’s what I want." SUPREME COURT TEMPORARILY BLOCKS APPEALS COURT RULING ON ABORTION PILL, RESTORES WIDER ACCESS TO DRUG Rodrigo released her song "Serena Joy" just before the festival. The single is named after a character from "Handmaid’s Tale" who promoted an oppressive regime that eventually deprived her of her own power. Lyrics including "a tower we built, painted gold on the walls" and "now go bother your neighbors while we do what we wish" have prompted speculation that the song takes aim at President Donald Trump, though Rodrigo declined to confirm that interpretation. "It’s basically a song about complacency," the singer said. "It’s about how an attack on one person’s human rights is an attack on all of our human rights. It’s something I’ve been thinking about a lot." Rodrigo's decision to incorporate politics into her performances drew praise and criticism from political commentators, some of whom argued that her approach alienates fans who do not share her views. Podcast host Ben Ferguson told Fox News Digital that the festival represented the "breathtaking hypocrisy of Hollywood," arguing that Rodrigo was treating her audience like "political minions." SPRINGSTEEN, OTHER STARS SHARE STAGE WITH HARDCORE LEFTIST GROUPS AT MUSIC FEST "These celebrities love preaching tolerance, diversity, and inclusion right up until someone dares to disagree with their politics. Then suddenly it’s, ‘Don’t buy a ticket.’ Apparently, everyone is welcome as long as they think exactly like Olivia Rodrigo," Ferguson said. "That’s not inclusion. That’s political arrogance wrapped in a concert tour." But Rodrigo’s willingness to openly embrace politics has also won praise from Democrats, including strategist Kaivan Shroff, who said celebrities who don’t speak out on current events can be viewed as "inauthentic." "This is not some niche artist trying to cultivate a fanbase by leaning into cheap politics. She is making politics part of the art, part of the live show and part of the brand, and at least she is being honest about that and owning it," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "I actually think ‘if you don’t agree, don’t buy a ticket’ is cleaner than pretending the politics are incidental. But there is a tradeoff," he continued. "The minute you tell people the show itself carries a political message, disagreement with that message becomes part of the consumer experience too. You cannot make politics central to the product and then act surprised when the product gets judged politically." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rodrigo has previously sparred with the Trump administration, condemning the Department of Homeland Security in 2025 after it used her song "All-American b----" in a social media post encouraging illegal immigrants to self-deport from the country. She has also criticized Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for being "barbaric and cruel." Film critic and Hollywood in Toto founder Christian Toto echoed Ferguson’s concerns, telling Fox News Digital: "In these contentious times, getting hyper political and alienating large swathes of your audience is less than ideal." Fox News Digital has reached out to the White House for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Joe Rogan and Spotify renew massive podcast deal
articles.summary: Spotify has renewed its licensing agreement with Joe Rogan. The lucrative deal will allow new episodes of The Joe Rogan Experience to appear across Spotify and other podcasting platforms.
articles.body: Spotify has renewed its licensing agreement with Joe Rogan, whose podcast remains the number one show on the platform — and in the world. As reported by The Wall Street Journal, the multi-year agreement is valued at around $250 million, allowing new episodes of The Joe Rogan Experience to appear on Spotify and across other platforms each week. The renewal builds on the lucrative relationship between Spotify and Rogan that began with an exclusive streaming agreement for The Joe Rogan Experience in 2020. The company later allowed the show to be distributed to YouTube, Apple, and other podcasting platforms as part of its 2024 deal with Rogan. The controversies surrounding Rogan’s show haven’t stopped Spotify from partnering with him. During the 2024 election season, the show became a campaign stop for high-profile politicians, including Donald Trump and JD Vance. “Six years later, JRE remains a defining show on Spotify, with a massive global audience and a format built around the wide-ranging, long-form conversations that have become its signature,” Spotify says in its announcement.
